title: The bomb that broke windows in Finland 💥
subject: explosion
description:
Should a weapon like this ever have been built? 👇

On October 30, 1961, the Soviet Union dropped the Tsar Bomba over Novaya Zemlya: 50 megatons, the most powerful explosion humans have ever set off. Its flash was seen about 1,000 km away and its shock wave circled the Earth 3 times.

Sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation, "Tsar Bomba"; Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, "Tsar Bomba" (2021); IFLScience, "Tsar Bomba: The Biggest Nuclear Bomb Ever Detonated" (cameraman quote via nuclearweaponarchive.org).

scenes.text: A fireball 5 miles wide hung over the Arctic.
October 30, 1961. A Soviet bomber dropped the Tsar Bomba over Novaya Zemlya.
50 megatons, about 1,570 times Hiroshima and Nagasaki combined. The cloud rose 40 miles.
The crew of pilot Andrei Durnovtsev had been given a 50 percent chance of surviving.
Windows shattered in Norway and Finland. A Soviet cameraman wrote, "The ball was powerful and arrogant like Jupiter."
The shock wave circled the Earth 3 times.
